findings.title: Two of the three v1 slice-level gates have no state, no insertion point and no slice
findings.description:
- **Scope count is wrong.** "V1 implements only the four slice-level transitions" (line 141), but the config lists three (`pre-tasks`, `pre-implementation`, `pre-advance`); the fourth, `pre-slice-plan`, is the deferred initiative-level one.
- **Only `pre-advance` is designed.** `pending-review` is defined as "tasks complete, … no review artifact present", and the single new branch sits between Priority 5 and 6. Anticipated Slices describe nothing else.
- **`pre-tasks` has no hook.** It would have to intercept Priority 4 (`needs-tasks`, `WorkflowNavigator.ts:224`), where `deriveSliceStatus()` returns before the proposed logic runs.
- **`pre-implementation` has no hook either.** A task file with zero boxes checked is already `in-implementation` (`:493`), so there is no "tasks exist, not started" state to gate. The document does not say what happens if the tasks review fails at 50% implemented.
- **One status cannot name the blocked transition.** A single `pending-review` / `review-failed` pair does not say which review type is missing.

Either cut v1 to `pre-advance` only, or specify the status values, cascade branches and "implementation started" rule for the other two. As written it cannot be slice-planned.

findings.title: The gate's machine-readable contract contradicts the design goal and the existing `NextAction` shape
findings.description:
- **Goal versus mechanism.** Design Goals say runners act "without parsing recommendation strings". Related Work says the gate "must not change the `NextAction` return type, only add new `recommendation` string values".
- **No stable vocabulary exists.** `recommendation` today is display prose, e.g. `` `Continue implementation — ${remaining} tasks remaining` `` and `` `Advance to slice ${nextEntry.index}: ${nextEntry.name}` ``. There is no `advance` token for `review` / `blocked` to sit beside. Adding two bare tokens to a prose field makes a user-facing label into logic, which CLAUDE.md prohibits.
- **Routing data is only in prose.** The review type and transition a runner needs appear only inside `rationale` ("(type: code)").
- **The `auto_advance` argument rests on nothing.** `workflow.auto_advance` is defined in `ConfigKeys.ts` and read nowhere in `packages/`, so "the gate naturally takes precedence" describes a consumer that does not exist.

Add optional structured fields to `NextAction` (e.g. `gate: { transition, reviewType, state, verdict }`). That is additive and removes the string dependency.

findings.title: Config plumbing is assumed, not designed; three claims are false against `ConfigManager`
findings.description:
- **Navigator and checker have no config access.** `WorkflowNavigator` is built as `new WorkflowNavigator()` with `getNext(project)`. `ConsistencyChecker` takes only an introspector, and `workflow.auto_fix` is read at the surface (`cli/src/commands/check.ts:140`). So "both surfaces inherit it without per-surface work" is wrong: the call sites in `next.ts`, `status.ts` and `workflowTools.ts` must change, or core classes must construct their own `ConfigManager`. The injection seam is unspecified.
- **`validate` does not run on read.** `validateValue()` is called only from `ConfigManager.set()`. `get()` returns whatever is in the TOML, cast to `string | boolean | number`. A hand-edited `review_threshold = "bogus"` (the documented way to write `[workflow.review_gates]`) is never validated, so the "fail-fast on configuration errors" principle has no enforcement point.
- **Nested tables do not fit the registry.** `get()` throws `Unknown config key` for anything not in `CONFIG_KEYS`, and the definition type is scalar-only. The hyphenated, inline-table `review_gates` shape is a config-system extension, deferred to "slice design time". That contradicts "following the existing pattern" and "no 160 interfaces change".
- **Worktree-scoped config does not exist.** Resolution is project → user → default (`ConfigManager.ts:91-130`). Related Work says to use "the resolution chain 180 introduced"; 180's overlay applies to project fields, not config.

findings.title: Config value domains and the enabled-with-no-gates case are undefined
findings.description:
- **`review_threshold` has no enumerated domain.** `"concerns"` and `"pass"` appear; "clears if `review_threshold = "concerns"` or lower" implies a third value that is never named.
- **`review_unknown_as` is inconsistent.** It is `"fail"` at line 75, `"concern"` (singular, versus `CONCERNS` / `"concerns"`) at line 147, and line 106 implies a "treats it as pending" value.
- **UNKNOWN maps to different statuses in different sections.** Line 106 puts it in `pending-review`; under the default `fail` policy it would be `review-failed` / `blocked`.
- **Default gate set is unstated.** `review_gates` is "optional overrides", yet line 111 says with "no gate configured for the current transition" nothing is set. With `review_enabled = true` and no table, it is unclear whether zero, one or all transitions are gated, or which `reviewType` applies.
- **UNKNOWN is common in practice.** Real Squadron artifacts carry `verdict: UNKNOWN` with `status: complete` (e.g. `244-review.slice.conditional-persistent-session-construction.md`). The default policy turns those into `blocked` with no route to re-review.

findings.title: Read and parse failures are folded into a policy that can pass them, and existing code swallows them first
findings.description:
- **Unreadable files can clear the gate.** A malformed or unreadable review "must not silently pass", but it becomes `UNKNOWN` and goes through `review_unknown_as`. With `"concern"` and threshold `concerns`, a permission-denied file clears. I/O failure needs to be distinct from a reviewer-emitted `UNKNOWN`.
- **The parser cannot report the failure.** `parseFrontmatter()` "never throws" and returns `{ found: false }` for ENOENT, EACCES, a missing closing `---` and no frontmatter alike. "The rationale … names the parse failure explicitly" is not achievable with the machinery the design reuses.
- **Nested YAML is flattened.** The parser is line-based and last-wins. Real artifacts have nested `criteria:` and `findings:` blocks whose child keys land at top level, so any nested `verdict`, `score` or `status` key would overwrite the real one. No YAML parser or real-artifact fixture is called for.
- **Exceptions become "no active slice".** `deriveSliceStatus()` ends in `catch { return base; }` (`WorkflowNavigator.ts:494`). An error in gate code placed there yields "Pick your first slice", not a gate error.

findings.title: Review discovery model does not fit the artifacts or the detector
findings.description:
- **One slot, several review types.** A slice can need `slice`, `tasks` and `code` reviews at once. Having `detectDocuments(projectPath, sliceIndex)` filter by "configured reviewType" pushes policy into a detector that takes no config today. Return reviews keyed by type and let the gate choose.
- **"Lexicographically last (most recent by sort order)" is unfounded.** Filenames carry no date or sequence. A re-review saved under a different suffix is ordered alphabetically, so a stale FAIL or PASS can win. Real names include `919-review.tasks.verification-that-verified-nothing.part-2.md`. Use `dateUpdated`, or treat duplicates as a `cf check` error.
- **The cited convention is not in this repo.** There is no `project-documents/user/reviews/` directory and no `210-review.code.…` file here. `frontmatterSchema.ts:97-105` defines `review` without `verdict`.
- **Dotted review types exist.** Squadron emits `302-review.judge.slice-vs-arch.….md`; these are the only artifacts I found carrying `score`. I did not find a slice 300 contract document to check the schema against.
- **Freshness is not addressed.** A PASS written before later task or code changes still clears the gate.

findings.title: ConsistencyChecker rule conflicts with existing auto-fix rules and has no baseline for existing slices
findings.description:
- **Two definitions of "complete".** The checker rule keys on "marked complete in the slice plan"; the navigator gate keys on task checkboxes.
- **Auto-fix can contradict the gate.** `task-vs-plan` (`ConsistencyChecker.ts:269-282`) is fixable and, under `workflow.auto_fix`, checks the plan box as soon as tasks are complete. A `review-failed` slice gets marked done in the plan, then the new rule raises a non-fixable `error` on it. `frontmatter-vs-computed` does the same for `status`. The document should say whether these fixes are suppressed while the gate is uncleared.
- **No baseline for history.** `checkAll()` iterates every plan entry. This project has about 170 completed slices and no review artifacts, so enabling `review_enabled` floods `cf check` with warnings. No cutoff is defined.

findings.title: v1 carries mechanisms nothing uses yet
findings.description:
The document is `riskLevel: low` and the gate is "read a field, compare to a threshold". Cut or defer:

- **Per-transition `review_gates` table.** It forces the config-system extension above; v1 can be `review_enabled` plus `review_threshold` on `pre-advance` with a fixed `code` review type.
- **`pre-slice-plan` in the v1 schema.** It is accepted in config but has no gate logic, so a user who sets it gets a silent no-op. Reject it until its slice ships.
- **Score "read and stored".** There is nowhere to store it, and the "documented code path" for a later switch is dead code.
- **"Carrying" `criteria` and `provenance`.** CF never writes review artifacts, and `FrontmatterData` is `Record<string, string>`, which cannot hold a nested dict.
- **Worktree-scoped resolution of `workflow.review_*`.** It needs a config scope that does not exist.

findings.title: Slice sequencing inconsistencies
findings.description:
- Technical Considerations puts the priority renumbering in "the slice implementing the gate logic"; Anticipated Slices puts it in slice 1, which has "no gate logic yet".
- Slice 1 (detector slot plus config keys) has no consumer and no observable behaviour, so it is a horizontal layer; merge it with the gate slice.
- `SliceStatus.status` is an inline string union (`types.ts:257`), not an enum. Extract it to a single `as const` definition, since `status.ts`, `buildSummary()` and the cascade all compare against it.

findings.title: `review-failed` has no exit expressible in CF
findings.description: Reconciliation is "above CF's layer", and truth is artifact-only. A human who accepts the findings can only hand-edit Squadron's `verdict` field or turn gating off project-wide. State that this is intended, or name the artifact that records a waiver.
